artists.biography: The Wannadies were an alternative rock band formed in 1988 in Skellefteå, Sweden.  The bands initial line-up featured Pär Wiksten (vocals, guitars), Christina Bergmark (keyboards, vocals), Stefan Schönfeldt (guitars) and his younger brother Frederick Schönfeldt (bass) with Gunnar Karlsson (drums) and Björn Malmquist (violin). Karlsson was later replaced by Erik Dahlgren.  Early influences included Australian band The Go-Betweens as well as The Sisters of Mercy.  The band released six studio albums in their 21 year career including the commercially successful Be A Girl (1994) and Bagsy Me (1997).  Part-way through recording their seventh studio album the band officially announced their split in April 2009 with Pär Wiksten going solo.

perplexity.description:
Be a Girl" is the third studio album by Swedish rock band The Wannadies, originally released in 1994. The album is a defining work in their discography, showcasing their signature blend of melodic guitar-driven rock with catchy hooks and a distinctly Scandinavian pop sensibility. Produced primarily by Nille Perned, the album features a polished yet energetic sound, with standout tracks like "Love in June" highlighting the band's knack for crafting memorable singles. The music balances upbeat rhythms with introspective lyrics, reflecting the band's evolution from their earlier indie roots to a more refined pop-rock style.

Released on Indolent Records, "Be a Girl" marked a turning point for The Wannadies, gaining them wider recognition both in Sweden and internationally. The album's success helped establish the band as key figures in the Scandinavian rock scene of the 1990s. While it did not achieve massive commercial chart success, it received positive critical attention for its songwriting and production, and remains a fan favorite. Its influence can be heard in the band's subsequent releases, cementing "Be a Girl" as an important milestone in their career.
